description: Defines the canonical identifiers, shared object contracts, relationship conventions, provenance requirements, temporal rules, confidence representation, and interoperability requirements used across A.R.I.A. services.

core_principle.statement: Every ARIA engine may reason differently, but all engines shall exchange information through stable canonical contracts. Shared concepts shall have one authoritative semantic meaning regardless of which service creates, reads, modifies, or references them.
rules: Canonical identifiers shall be globally unique within their entity class.
Shared entities shall not be independently redefined by individual engines.
Relationships shall reference canonical identifiers rather than duplicated embedded objects whenever practical.
Provenance shall travel with technical information.
Confidence shall remain distinguishable from probability.
Unknown values shall remain distinguishable from null, false, zero, and not applicable.
Historical records shall preserve temporal context.
Entity contracts shall be extensible without requiring destructive schema redesign.
Manufacturers, products, users, scopes, technologies, and future domains shall be added through entities and relationships rather than hard-coded directory depth.
Backward compatibility shall be preserved whenever practical.
Human-readable names shall never serve as primary identifiers.
Renaming an entity shall not change its identifier.
Manufacturer part numbers and external IDs shall be aliases rather than canonical ARIA IDs.
Deleted or retired identifiers shall not be reused.

status_contract.rule: Domain-specific status values may extend common statuses but shall not silently redefine them.

rules: UNKNOWN shall not be represented as zero.
UNKNOWN shall not be represented as false.
NOT_APPLICABLE shall remain distinct from UNKNOWN.
NOT_OBSERVED shall remain distinct from confirmed absence.
Engines shall preserve unknown-state semantics during serialization and retrieval.
Observation time and record creation time shall remain distinguishable.
Historical technical information shall preserve when it was true or observed.
Current applicability shall not be inferred solely from record modification time.
Time-sensitive technical relationships may define effective intervals.
Confidence shall represent trust in a claim, interpretation, probability, or decision.
Confidence shall not be substituted for probability.
Confidence values shall retain their basis when practical.
Probability represents relative or absolute likelihood according to the applicable model.
Probability shall not independently imply certainty.
Competing normalized hypotheses shall identify their normalization group.
Derived information shall reference the information from which it was derived.
Copying information between systems shall not create independent provenance.
Original source lineage shall remain recoverable whenever practical.
Relationships shall be first-class objects when they contain technical meaning.
A relationship may carry context, confidence, provenance, and temporal applicability.
Reverse relationships shall not be assumed unless defined by semantics.
New relationship types may be added without reorganizing physical directories.
User identity shall remain separate from user experience history.
User-specific learning shall reference the canonical user_id.
User overlays shall modify reasoning context without duplicating the global knowledge graph.
Products shall reference manufacturers rather than exist inside manufacturer-specific reasoning trees.
Products may participate in unlimited scopes and relationships.
Adding a new product shall not require creating a new reasoning engine.

technology_entity.rule: Technology is an orthogonal dimension and shall not be encoded solely through manufacturer or product hierarchy.

scope_entity.rule: The same technical concept may participate in multiple scopes without duplication.

failure_mode_entity.rule: Failure modes shall exist independently of manufacturer-specific implementations unless the failure mechanism is truly manufacturer-specific.

rules: Values and units shall be stored separately.
Directionality shall be explicit when technically relevant.
Measurement context shall remain attached to the measurement.

action_entity.rule: An action definition is distinct from an action instance performed within a case.

state_version_entity.rule: State versions are immutable after commit.

experience_entity.rule: Experience shall be multidimensionally scoped rather than stored as duplicated user-specific copies of the global knowledge graph.

context_signature.description: A compact multidimensional description of the technical environment applicable to an observation, hypothesis, action, experience, or knowledge relationship.
rules: Dimensions may be absent when unknown or irrelevant.
Context matching shall not require every dimension to match.
More specific context may inherit applicable broader knowledge.
Context specificity shall be considered when ranking retrieved information.

knowledge_edge_contract.rule: Knowledge edges carry meaning and may be traversed across multiple conceptual dimensions.

anti_duplication_policy.description: Prevents the directory and knowledge model from reproducing the same technical concept in every manufacturer, product, user, and troubleshooting branch.
rules: Create the concept once.
Represent applicability through relationships.
Manufacturer-specific behavior shall extend the canonical concept rather than duplicate it.
User-specific history shall reference canonical concepts rather than copy them.
Scope-specific procedures shall reference shared technical entities.

growth_policy.description: Defines how ARIA absorbs future manufacturers, products, technologies, and scopes.

steps: Add only genuinely new technical concepts.
Do not create a new reasoning hierarchy.

growth_policy.rule: Adding products expands the graph; it shall not deepen an ever-growing directory tree.

rules: API payloads shall include schema_version.
Unknown fields should be tolerated when safe to support forward compatibility.
Breaking semantic changes require a new major schema version.
Identifiers shall remain stable across serialization formats.
Additive optional fields normally constitute backward-compatible changes.
Changing the meaning of an existing field is a breaking change.
Removing required fields is a breaking change.
Migration logic shall preserve historical records.
Historical entities shall remain interpretable according to the schema version under which they were created.

contract_validation.rule: Invalid inter-engine payloads shall be rejected before authoritative state mutation.

relationships: RF Routing Error MAY_CAUSE RSL Degradation
example_graph.interpretation: The graph can grow in every direction without requiring Nokia/UBT/UBT-T/18GHz/troubleshooting/RSL directories or duplicated user-specific knowledge trees.

semantic_rules.rule: Shared ARIA concepts shall have one canonical semantic definition.
Canonical identifiers shall remain stable when names, locations, or relationships change.
Human-readable names shall not serve as authoritative identity.
Provenance shall remain attached to technical information across engine boundaries.
Probability and confidence shall remain separate contract types.
Unknown, absent, false, zero, and not applicable shall remain semantically distinct.
Observation time and record creation time shall remain distinct.
Relationships containing technical meaning shall be represented explicitly.
Products shall be graph entities rather than directory structures.
Technologies and scopes shall remain orthogonal dimensions.
Failure modes shall be canonical concepts rather than duplicated manufacturer-specific labels unless technically unique.
User-specific experience shall reference global canonical concepts rather than duplicate the knowledge graph.
Adding a manufacturer or product shall expand relationships rather than require new reasoning architecture.
Context shall be multidimensional rather than encoded through directory depth.
More-specific context may inherit applicable broader knowledge.
Action definitions and performed action instances shall remain distinct.
Historical state versions and events shall remain immutable.
Inter-engine payloads shall be schema validated before authoritative state mutation.
Schema evolution shall preserve historical interpretability.
ARIA's information architecture shall grow as an interconnected graph rather than an increasingly deep tree.
